content: Rifater, a combination of rifampin, isoniazid, and pyrazinamide, is contraindicated in patients who have a history of hypersensitivity to rifampin, isoniazid, pyrazinamide, any of the components of the medication, or any of the rifamycin class of antibiotics. Rifampin is contraindicated in patients who are concurrently receiving ritonavir-boosted saquinavir due to the increased risk of severe hepatocellular toxicity. Additionally, rifampin should not be used in patients who are taking atazanavir, darunavir, fosamprenavir, saquinavir, or tipranavir because rifampin can significantly reduce the plasma concentrations of these antiviral drugs. This reduction may lead to a loss of antiviral efficacy and/or the development of viral resistance. Isoniazid is contraindicated in patients with severe hepatic damage, those who have experienced severe adverse reactions to isoniazid (such as drug fever, chills, or arthritis), patients with acute liver disease of any etiology, and those with acute gout.
